rendered: The premise is not supported: the 50%[1] Mn-doped LNO did not deliver more capacity. The document reports lower discharge capacity for that sample: 212 mAh g^− 1 (10% Mn) vs 164 mAh g^− 1[2]. So the 10%[3] Mn sample had the higher capacity, and the 50%[4] Mn sample released less heat, not more. The thermal tests report 901.4 J g^−1 for 10% Mn[5] versus 485.7 J g^−1 for 50% Mn[6]. The 10%[7] Mn sample therefore released about 415.7[8] J/g more heat than the 50%[9] Mn sample, the reverse of the premise. The paper attributes this to lower-Mn systems generating comparatively more heat in these tests, so higher Mn content gave less heat release.
